messages:
kai: Observed a steady p95/throughput regression after canary rollout to v5.0.0 in the midnight window (started ~00:10 UTC). Canary was at 15%.
amy: deploybot shows: "rollout v5.0.0 canary=15% region=global started 00:08". Any auto-revert triggers?
deploybot: auto-signal: p95 > threshold for 5m on /v1/generate. Autorevert policy: alert-only in change window.
pavel: logs show repeated retry spikes and a new exception class `cache_miss_spike`. Dedicated pools show higher cpu and GC churn.
rachel: do we let autorevert run or take manual action? We have two large enterprise dedicated customers on that pool.
kai: manual. We want traces preserved and targeted traffic control. Plan: 1) soft traffic unwind for dedicated pool only (15%->0% over 4m) 2) pin previous stable v4.9.2 for dedicated 3) open infra rollback PR 4) collect 30m traces 5) decide rollforward vs hard revert.
ops-bert: Command ready: `rictl traffic shift --service generator --from v5.0.0 --to v4.9.2 --percent 15 --scope dedicated --duration 240s`
lee-sre: also capture `allocstats`, `kv_cache_miss` counters, and runtime kernel flags while unwinding.
monica-product: I'll prepare a targeted customer note and update release notes if we pin. Keep wording: factual and non-alarming.
amy: executing traffic shift now. Response: ok shifting 15->0 over 240s (dedicated only).
deploybot: update: canary at 12% per rollout plan.
(2m)
pavel: p95 dropping as traffic leaves dedicated nodes. Error spikes halving at 8% canary.
lee-sre: good. Keep draining; hold before we touch hosted traffic.
(5m)
amy: canary for dedicated drained to 0%. Hosted remains at 15% paused/halted.
ops-bert: pinning version now: `rictl pin version --service generator --version v4.9.2 --scope dedicated --note "after canary unwind 00:20 UTC"` -> ok.
monica-product: drafted customer blurb: "During our scheduled maintenance window, we observed elevated latency on generation endpoints in dedicated pools. Traffic was shifted back to a stable version; customers on dedicated pools were routed to the stable version. We are investigating root cause and will follow up."
kai: created rollback PR to revert canary manifests: https://git.internal/infra/pull/5022 (WIP). Tagging pavel and lee-sre.
pavel: starting trace aggregation for 30m. Early signs: kernel fallback to quant_path_v1 on long context leads to kv cache churn.
lee-sre: if traces confirm kernel fallback as culprit, remediation options: kernel guard (disable quant_path_v1), canary flag to gate long-context paths, or revert until patch.
monica-product: legal checked; no SLA escalation required now. Support should have the note ready.
(20m)
pavel: preliminary RCA notes: kernel selection regression in v5.0.0 when sequence length > 1024 leads to cache miss amplification and higher per-token CPU. Draft PM in #postmortems.
amy: merging rollback PR to ensure infra manifests reflect stable baseline.
deploybot: PR merged; canary manifests reverted to v4.9.2 for dedicated.
lee-sre: recommend keep dedicated pinned for 24h, run compatibility tests and a focused canary with kernel guard.
ops-bert: scheduling patch rollout for next change window.
monica-product: sent customer note to affected list at 01:05 UTC. Release notes updated with rollback steps and commands.
kai: closing immediate ops thread. Follow-ups: pavel (RCA doc), lee-sre (test plan), ops-bert (patch ticket), monica-product (customer comms). If any metric regresses we'll escalate to hard revert and open oncall bridge.
rachel: thanks team. :thumbsup:
